name: Apple MacBook Air 13" (M5, 2026)
verdict: The best laptop for most people — Apple's M5 chip, 16GB of memory, and a fanless design in a 13-inch body that goes anywhere.
description: The 13-inch MacBook Air is the laptop we'd hand to almost anyone. The M5 chip is far more power than everyday work demands, and like every Apple-silicon Air it has no fan, so it stays completely silent whether you're writing, editing photos, or on a video call. This configuration gets the important things right: 16GB of unified memory and a 512GB SSD, so you won't outgrow it in a year. The 13.6-inch Liquid Retina display is sharp and bright, the 12MP Center Stage camera keeps you framed on calls, and Wi-Fi 7 future-proofs it for newer routers.
pros: Fanless and silent under any workload
16GB memory and 512GB storage out of the box
Center Stage camera is great for calls
cons: 13-inch screen feels tight for side-by-side windows

name: Apple MacBook Air 15" (M5, 2026)
verdict: Everything we love about the 13-inch Air, with a roomy 15.3-inch screen for spreadsheets, editing, and two apps side by side.
description: If you like the MacBook Air but want more screen, the 15-inch model is the one. You get the same M5 chip, 16GB of memory, and 512GB SSD as the 13-inch, with a 15.3-inch Liquid Retina display that makes split-screen work and photo editing far more comfortable. It's still fanless and silent, and still thin enough to slide into a work bag. The trade-off is simply size: it takes up more of a café table and a bit more of your backpack.
pros: Big, bright screen in a thin body
Same strong memory and storage as the 13-inch

name: ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED (Ryzen AI 9 465)
verdict: Our favorite Windows ultralight — a vivid 2K OLED touchscreen, Ryzen AI 9 power, and a full 1TB of storage.
description: The Zenbook 14 OLED is the Windows laptop we'd pick for people who carry their computer everywhere. Its 2K OLED touchscreen hits 500 nits with HDR, so colors pop and blacks are truly black. The AMD Ryzen AI 9 465 is a Copilot+ chip with plenty of headroom for multitasking, and 16GB of RAM with a 1TB SSD is a generous configuration. It ships with Windows 11 Pro and a backlit keyboard, which makes it an easy fit for work as well as home.
cons: Glossy OLED can reflect in bright rooms
16GB RAM isn't upgradeable on most ultralights

name: Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14
verdict: The business laptop to beat — 32GB of fast memory, a 2.8K 120Hz OLED, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, and that ThinkPad keyboard.
description: The X1 Carbon is the laptop IT departments and frequent flyers trust, and Gen 14 keeps it at the top. This configuration pairs an Intel Core Ultra 5 335 with vPro management features and a generous 32GB of LPDDR5X memory, so heavy browser and spreadsheet loads never bog it down. The 14-inch 2.8K OLED runs at up to 120Hz for smooth scrolling, and three Thunderbolt 4 ports mean you can dock to monitors without a mess of dongles. The keyboard remains one of the best you can type on.
pros: 32GB of memory is rare at this level
cons: 512GB SSD fills up fast for media

name: ASUS ROG Zephyrus G14 (RTX 5080)
verdict: The most powerful laptop you can still carry comfortably — RTX 5080 graphics and a 3K 120Hz OLED in a 14-inch chassis.
description: The Zephyrus G14 packs serious gaming and creative muscle into a laptop that doesn't look or feel like a brick. The GeForce RTX 5080 with 16GB of GDDR7 handles modern games and GPU-heavy editing, while the AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, 32GB of RAM, and 2TB SSD keep everything else fast. The 14-inch 3K OLED at 120Hz is stunning for both games and color work. It's VR-ready, ships with Windows 11 Pro, and has an RGB backlit keyboard.
cons: Fans get loud under full load
Battery life drops fast while gaming

name: Acer Chromebook Plus 514
verdict: The best laptop for tight budgets and students — a fast Chromebook Plus with a 14-inch touchscreen and Google AI built in.
description: If most of what you do happens in a browser, the Chromebook Plus 514 is the smartest money you can spend on a laptop. The Intel Core i3-1315U and 8GB of LPDDR5 memory meet Google's Chromebook Plus performance bar, so it stays quick with lots of tabs open. The 14-inch 1920×1080 IPS touchscreen has a matte finish that's easy on the eyes, the FHD camera is a step up for video calls, and Wi-Fi 7 is a surprise at this level. ChromeOS updates itself and is very hard to slow down with clutter.
cons: Can't run full Windows or Mac apps
Not built for gaming or video editing

name: Microsoft Surface Laptop 7 (13.8")
verdict: A premium, all-day Windows laptop — Snapdragon X Plus, a 120Hz touchscreen, and 1TB of storage in a beautifully built shell.
description: Surface Laptop 7 is Microsoft's answer to the MacBook Air, and it's a good one. The Snapdragon X Plus chip is a Copilot+ processor built for long battery life, and this configuration's 16GB of memory and 1TB SSD are generous. The 13.8-inch 2K+ touchscreen runs at 120Hz, the 1080p IR webcam supports Windows Hello face login, and the backlit keyboard is excellent. It's a great pick for people who want Windows with the polish and battery life of a premium ultraportable.
cons: A few older Windows apps and games don't run on ARM chips

name: Lenovo Yoga 7i 2-in-1 16" (2026)
verdict: The best 2-in-1 — a big 16-inch 2K touchscreen that folds into a tablet, with 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage.
description: The Yoga 7i folds 360 degrees, so the same machine works as a laptop, a tent for watching shows, or a big tablet for sketching and note-taking. Its 16-inch 2K touchscreen is roomy enough for real work, and the Intel Core Ultra 5 322 includes a 46 TOPS NPU for Copilot+ features. With 16GB of LPDDR5X memory, a 1TB SSD, Windows 11 Pro, a fingerprint reader, and Wi-Fi 7, it's well equipped for school or home.
cons: Heavy to use as a handheld tablet

name: Acer Aspire Go 15 (Core 3 N355)
verdict: A basic Windows laptop for email, browsing, and schoolwork — a full-size 15.6-inch screen at a very low price.
description: The Aspire Go 15 is for people who need Windows and a big screen without spending much. The 15.6-inch 1920×1080 IPS display is comfortable for documents and video, and the Intel Core 3 N355 handles email, web browsing, and streaming. Expectations matter here: 8GB of memory and 128GB of storage are minimal, so it's best for light, focused use. It ships in Windows 11 S mode, which you can switch off for free if you need to install apps outside the Microsoft Store.
pros: Fine for email, browsing, and streaming
cons: Ships in S mode (free to switch off)

name: Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i 15.6" (with Microsoft Office)
verdict: An entry-level 15.6-inch Windows laptop that comes with Microsoft Office and 1TB of cloud storage included.
description: The IdeaPad Slim 3i is a simple, slim Windows laptop aimed at households and students who mainly need Office apps. Its selling point is the bundle: Microsoft Office and 1TB of cloud storage are included, which covers documents, spreadsheets, and backups without an extra purchase. The 15.6-inch FHD display is comfortable for everyday work. The 128GB SSD is small, so plan on keeping files in the included cloud storage.
cons: Not for gaming or creative apps
